positions.name: Global X Uranium ETF
positions.thesis: The purest listed claim on the fuel bottleneck. Holds miners and enrichers, so it captures the spot uranium move with equity beta stacked on top.
positions.breaks: A restart of idled Kazakh and Namibian supply, or one high-profile reactor incident, resets sentiment far faster than mine supply can respond.

positions.name: VanEck Uranium & Nuclear ETF
positions.thesis: Deliberately the boring half of the sleeve. Weighted toward utilities and reactor builders rather than juniors, it earns cash while URA takes the risk.
positions.breaks: It is not really a uranium proxy — the utility weighting means it can drift with rates while the actual fuel thesis plays out.

positions.name: Petrobras PN
positions.thesis: Pre-salt barrels at a single-digit multiple with a double-digit payout. Priced for permanent political risk, which is a real risk that is nonetheless already in the number.
positions.breaks: Dividend policy is set by the controlling shareholder, and the controlling shareholder is the state. Fuel-price intervention ahead of an election ends the thesis without warning.

positions.name: Saudi Aramco
positions.thesis: The lowest-cost barrel on earth and the swing producer that sets the floor. Owned here as the stabiliser of the sleeve, not for its growth.
positions.breaks: Free float is thin and the payout leans on the state budget. A sustained sub-$60 Brent forces a choice between the dividend and Vision 2030.

positions.name: LandBridge Company
positions.thesis: The hinge of the whole book. Owns Permian surface acreage and collects royalties on whatever sits on it — water handling, pipelines, and now data-centre leases. Sells energy and compute demand without drilling or buying a GPU.
positions.breaks: Small float, and the data-centre revenue is a handful of contracts. Concentration cuts both ways, as a 9.5% single-session drop on 12 Aug demonstrated.

positions.name: ASUSTeK Computer
positions.thesis: AI server exposure at a hardware multiple rather than a semiconductor one. The AI server business is repricing the whole company while it is still classified as a PC maker.
positions.breaks: Server assembly is a margin-thin business with real customer concentration, and the legacy PC cycle still swamps the AI line in reported revenue.

positions.name: KOSPI Composite
positions.thesis: Country-level exposure to memory. HBM pricing runs through Korean national accounts, and the index carries a persistent governance discount that is finally being addressed.
positions.breaks: Not directly investable — it is an index, so a real book expresses it through a fund or futures and eats tracking error and FX. Also a first-order casualty of any Taiwan Strait event.

positions.name: Palantir Technologies
positions.thesis: The application layer. Sells the deployment of models into government and commercial workflows, which is where the margin sits once inference is a commodity.
positions.breaks: The multiple is the position. Growth is real and accelerating, but at this valuation a single decelerating quarter costs more than the growth adds.

positions.name: Anthropic

manualMark.basis: Series H, $65bn raised, led by Altimeter / Dragoneer / Greenoaks / Sequoia
manualMark.note: Confidential IPO filing 1 Jun 2026. No public market; carried flat at the last primary round.

positions.thesis: Direct exposure to the frontier lab whose demand curve the other three sleeves are ultimately serving. Held to make the book's central assumption explicit rather than implied.
positions.breaks: Illiquid and marked at a stale round, so the position understates its own volatility. A down round or a broken IPO would reprice it in one step, with no path to exit in between.

positions.name: iShares AI Infrastructure UCITS ETF
positions.thesis: Diversifies the single-name compute risk across semis, cloud and networking, so the sleeve survives being wrong about any one company.
positions.breaks: Heavy overlap with the megacap complex most portfolios already own, and the LSE line quotes GBP against a USD NAV — an FX layer sitting on top of the actual exposure.

positions.name: Gold — COMEX Dec 2026
positions.thesis: The hedge against the financing of everything above. If the energy and compute build-out is funded by deficits and suppressed real rates, gold is the direct expression of that.
positions.breaks: A dated future, not bullion — it expires 29 Dec 2026 and must be rolled, so the position carries basis and roll cost that a spot holding does not.

positions.name: Avantis International Small Cap Value ETF
positions.thesis: The deliberate opposite of the rest of the book: ex-US, small, cheap, profitable, and largely unowned by the AI trade. It is here to be uncorrelated, not to be exciting.
positions.breaks: Value has underperformed growth for most of a decade. If the AI build-out simply keeps compounding, this sleeve is a permanent drag on returns.
